What is a permission boundary and what is it for?

It is a managed policy that you attach to a user or a role (not a group) to set the maximum permissions it can obtain. It grants nothing: effective permissions are the intersection of the identity policy and the boundary. Use case: delegating user creation or policy management to non-admins without privilege escalation, by requiring the boundary via the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition. It can be combined with SCPs.
users and roles
How does evaluation work between an account A and an account B?

For cross-account access, both sides must authorize: the requester in account A must have an Allow in their identity-based policy toward the resource in account B, and account B's resource-based policy must authorize this requester. Within the same account, a single one of the two Allows is enough. In every case an explicit Deny wins, and SCP, boundary, and session policy only limit.

IAM role or resource-based policy for cross-account access?

With a role, you give up your original permissions for those of the role; they are temporary and suited to many actions in the other account. With a resource-based policy (S3, SNS, SQS...), the principal keeps its permissions and the authorization is permanent as long as the policy exists. Example: scanning DynamoDB in A and writing to S3 in B is better done with a bucket policy, so as not to lose your rights on DynamoDB.
